recipes.name: Slow Cooker Chicken Marrakesh
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
1 (15 ounce) can garbanzo beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Place chicken, sweet potatoes, garbanzo beans, carrots, onion, and garlic into a slow cooker.
Mix parsley, salt, cumin, turmeric, cinnamon, and pepper together in a small bowl. Sprinkle over chicken and vegetables, then pour in tomatoes and stir to combine.
Cover and cook on High until sweet potatoes are tender and sauce has thickened, 4 to 5 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Chicken Marrakesh
raw_recipe.description: This hearty chicken Marrakesh stew features chicken, sweet potatoes, garbanzo beans, tomatoes, and spices that simmer to perfection in the slow cooker.

review.reviewBody: Excellent! A delicious, easy, healthy, and budget friendly one-dish meal. I made it as written. The flavors blended nicely and it smelled wonderful while it was cooking. I cooked it on high for just under 4 hours and stirred it initially and then stirred one about half way through to blend everything and distribute liquid and had no problem with the chicken breasts drying out. UPDATE: I made this again and added red and green bell peppers and broccoli slaw to increase the vegetables and I doubled the spices except salt. Since I increased the vegetables I decided to add another can of diced tomatoes and that was a mistake because then it added too much liquid. I recommend not adding additional liquid even though it may look dry in the beginning because it makes its own sauce as it cooks. Also, this time it seemed the additional liquid diluted the spices as it was not as flavorful as the first time even though I doubled the spices this time. Next time I will add the additional vegetables but stick to 1 can of tomatoes and double the spices. It is a delicious recipe. If trying it for the first time I recommend following the recipe as written. UPDATE II: While eating leftovers of this recipe my husband declared this was the best dish I have made. So it is a winner.

Update….made this several times since my review & am making again today…funny as I only have black beans no chickpeas again…haha…this is a great tasty meal,especially for winter when soups/ stews are the best! I made this today & it was delicious. I only had black beans & they worked well. I used 1/2 boneless skinless chicken & 1/2 skinless chicken drums but next time I will use all drums or thighs as the dark meat is so much more flavorful. I also added a cup of chicken broth. A definite keeper...thanks for the recipe !

I followed the recipe for the most part. I doubled the spices as recommended by almost everybody. I also added allspice since cinnamon and turmeric were used. It definitely wasn’t salty. I usually am OK with this because others can salt to their taste. This was delicious. I put it on low for eight hours. My sweet potatoes we’re not mushy, but my carrots were still slightly crisp. Very pleased! So good!

Thank you "Occasional Cooker" for your tip. I tasted the broth after it had been cooking for a couple of hours and it was just ok. So I took your advice and added another batch of the seasonings except for the salt. I did that by grabbing my chicken base and making a broth, mixed in the seasonings and added that to the slow cooker. It turned out fabulous. The flavor is wonderful. I used chicken thighs because it's what I had on hand. Nice to find a recipe that I can happily add to my collection. It certainly was a nice change of pace too.
Doubled all of the spices and the garlic cloves, flavor was different but I enjoyed it. Cooked on low in instant pot for 3 hours.

It was super good. I used thighs but deboned and pulled the meat off then put it back in. Much better to me. Doubled all of the spices too Today going to make soup out of the broth. Thinking of adding more broth and maybe some more tomatoes. It’s a winner recipe

I love the flavor profile of this recipe but will definitely follow other reviewers' advice and double the spices next time, maybe also seeing if fresh parsley gives more flavor than dried. I'll probably also add more tomatoes and go for crushed instead of diced. Since I use a 4 qt crockpot, I'll chop the onion instead of slicing next time to save room. I'm new to cooking so these are my thoughts as a newbie.

As recommended by other reviewers; I used chicken thighs, doubled the spices (maybe a little more), and added a cup of chicken broth. I also threw in some sun dried tomatoes and used a little tapioca (2 T) to thicken it before serving. The flavor was great... And I'm all about tasting the spices! I served it over couscous.

Wowza! This is delicious! I doubled all the spices except the salt as suggested by others. I also put in a cup of chicken broth and about three tablespoons of butter. Someone else suggested the butter. I couldn't tell that it was necessary. I added the broth because I wanted to wind up with a soup and it worked well to that end. The next time I make this I will dice the onion. I think that form will work better for soup. I truly loved this recipe.

I leveled up the spices just a bit and also some red pepper flakes for added flavor. I drizzled olive oil in the pot, coating the chicken then sprinkled with spices, then added canned tomatoes. I didn't add the garbanzos and veggies until a couple hours before finish to keep from overcooking. Add additional fresh parsley when serving. Great with brown rice!
Tasty but spices were not strong enough for our tastes. Doubled the cinnamon and cumin and used smoky jalapeno (about 19 drops) from tabasco to provide a bit of bite with the smoky flavour
I love the flavor of this plus I have dysphasia and this is soft and easy to swallow! This is a win, win !!!

My husband and I tried this because a friend is a fan of foods from this region of the world, so this particular one said "easy". Typically we would not be drawn to this recipe but are pleased to say the flavors are wonderful and the presentation is colorful with a variety of ingredients. My tweaks out of the gate are adding a heaping tablespoon of butter into the bottom of the cooker, changed the garbonza beans to my preference for a can of small navy beans- these turned out to the best part of the recipe and added two packets of low sodium chicken bouillion. A value added is the aroma from the slow cooker filled our kitchen with a wonderful scent.
I've made this many times over the years and will make it again soon. Easy to assemble- mix and go. Lovely savory, mildly sweet flavors that keep you coming back for more.

The spices didn't look like nearly enough so we doubled them. I checked after two hours and could hardly taste the spices, so we added more. One can of tomatoes wasn't enough either, we put in two. At the two hour point there was nothing resembling a "sauce", so I added another can of tomatoes and a can of water. This recipe is promising, but I think it needs a lot of work.

Made as written and we loved the flavour. Next time I’ll add some raisins and switch out some/all of the chicken breast for dark meat. Thanks for the recipe. We’ve since made it many times, this is what worked for us: Doubled the entire recipe except for salt and pepper. If needed it can be added later. Used canned diced tomatoes and DRAINED them well, before adding, making the dish less runny. Added raisons, 1/2 - 1 cup depending on your tastes. We make it the day before, unplug it when it’s done, but leave everything in the slow cooker overnight. Reheat next day for our meal. Love it! We serve it with Moroccan Rice.
We have made this many times, but using bone in chicken thighs instead of chicken breast. We just find that the thighs don't dry out and have more flavor. Easy to make and very tasty!

I like the recipe in general, but I added A LOT more seasoning. I see people say they doubled it, I just eyeballed it but put probably 4xs as much of most seasonings. I also added chicken boullion and lots of garlic powder. It most definitely needs to be a dish made with a fattier meat. The chicken breast is too dry as happens with lean meats in a slow cooker. It would be an excellent dish to make with lamb, a whole chicken or maybe pork loin w fat on it. I think next time I’m going to try it with lamb chops. I also added a whole stick of butter at the end to moisten it up, and that made it SO MUCH BETTER. definitely add a stick of butter

I was looking for a new recipe to add to our rotation, and this one looked intriguing. I made it as directed only with fewer carrots, because the crockpot was really full. My husband and I liked it, but it seemed a little bland. I'll probably double the spices next time to get more of the flavor - it SMELLED really flavorful, but tasted a little bland. We just ate it as is, like a stew, but I might try over rice or couscous next time.
